patients.summary: Former security guard with diabetes and hypertension who joins in 2020 and is found to have HIV with a CD4 under 200 on screening. Poor antiretroviral adherence, then IgA nephropathy and FSGS with nephrotic syndrome and AKI on CKD 3; last seen September 2024, after which a run of opportunistic infections reaches the practice only as outside records.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32 y/o man establishing care. Previous PCP was across the river; he stopped going after his insurance changed to Medicaid and has been getting refills through urgent care. Records requested.

DM2 dx roughly 3 yrs ago, on metformin 1000 BID, says he takes it most days. No home glucose checks. HTN about 2 yrs, lisinopril 20 daily. Denies chest pain, SOB, vision change, foot numbness. No NSAID use.

PSH: appendectomy around age 22.
FHx: mother DM2 (dx at 45). Father HTN. Maternal uncle on dialysis, cause unknown.
SH: lives in Easthampton with partner. Unemployed, used to do security work. Smokes ~10/day since about 20. Alcohol a drink or two a month. No drugs.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 138/88. Well appearing. Fundi not dilated. Neck supple, no LAD. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, well-healed RLQ scar. Ext without edema. Feet intact to monofilament bilaterally, pulses 2+.

A/P
1. DM2 - A1c today. Continue metformin.
2. HTN - near goal, continue lisinopril 20. Recheck next visit.
3. Tobacco - advised quitting. He wants to cut down on his own, not ready for patches.
4. Health maintenance - CMP, CBC, lipids, UA, urine microalbumin. Offered routine HIV and hep C screening (one-time adult screening), he agreed. Flu shot at nurse visit in a couple weeks.
RTC 3 mo, sooner pending labs.

documents.title: Results discussed by phone
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt with screening results. HIV antigen/antibody screen is reactive. Explained this needs confirmation and a viral load and CD4 count. He was quiet, asked whether it could be wrong. Told him we confirm before calling it anything, but to take it seriously. He agreed to come in for blood work this afternoon and to come back Monday to go over everything in person.

Also: creatinine 1.5, which gives an eGFR right around 60, and urine microalbumin 380 with 1+ protein and 1+ blood on UA. A1c 7.1. Hep C antibody negative. Will repeat kidney tests in a few months; may need nephrology.

Advised condoms with partner until we have answers.

conditions.label: Human immunodeficiency virus disease
conditions.note: AIDS by CD4 under 200 at diagnosis

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - HIV Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over confirmatory testing. Came alone, partner waiting in the car.

HIV-1 RNA 85,000 copies/mL. CD4 140. This confirms HIV infection, and with a CD4 below 200 it meets the definition of AIDS. Spent most of the visit on what this means and does not mean: very treatable, one pill a day for most people, near-normal life expectancy when the virus is kept suppressed. He does not know when or how he acquired it; no prior test he can recall.

Denies fevers, sweats, thrush, rash, diarrhea, cough or headache today. Weight stable.

Exam: BP as charted. No oral thrush. No LAD. Skin clear. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. HIV disease, CD4 140 / VL 85k - urgent referral to the ID clinic at the regional hospital; front desk to call for first available. ID will start ART and prophylaxis. Discussed partner testing; he plans to tell his partner tonight and we can test the partner here or the partner's own doctor can. Condoms until suppressed.
2. Kidney labs - mild CKD picture with albuminuria. Will repeat in early 2021. Lisinopril helps here.
3. Gave crisis line and our after-hours number. He can text me.

f/u Jan, or sooner.

documents.title: Infectious Disease New Patient Consultation
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC, REGIONAL HOSPITAL
Date of visit: 11/23/2020
Referred by: primary care

Reason: newly diagnosed HIV-1.

33-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and hypertension found HIV-positive on routine screening at his new primary care practice in October. Baseline HIV-1 RNA 85,000 copies/mL, CD4 140 cells/mm3. No prior testing. Asymptomatic: no fever, weight loss, thrush, dysphagia, diarrhea, cough or headache.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
Social: lives with partner. Smokes about half a pack daily. Rare alcohol.

Exam: afebrile. Oropharynx clear. No lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear. Skin without lesions.

Assessment: HIV-1 infection, AIDS-defining by CD4 count.
Plan:
- Start bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 50/200/25 mg one tablet daily. Renal function adequate for this regimen; will follow creatinine.
- Start trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS one tablet daily for PCP prophylaxis while CD4 under 200.
- Genotype and remaining baseline labs drawn here; results will follow in our chart.
- Adherence counseling done with our pharmacist. Partner testing encouraged.
- Return in 4 weeks, then every 3 months.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: started the meds
documents.author: patient
documents.body: hey doc just letting you know I started the HIV pill and the antibiotic one a week and a half ago. stomach was a little off the first few days but fine now. my partner got tested at the clinic downtown and its negative. thank you for being straight with me

documents.title: RE: started the meds
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is really good news on both counts. Keep taking it every day, same time if you can - phone alarm helps. See you in January. Text me if anything comes up before then.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:

No fevers, rashes, diarrhea.

O: Vitals as charted. Lungs clear, RRR, no edema. Mouth clear.

A/P
DM2 - A1c and BMP today.
HTN - ok today, continue lisinopril 20.
Kidneys - repeat creatinine today; if still around 1.5-1.6 that is CKD 3a by eGFR with albuminuria. Will decide on nephrology after.
HIV - on bictegravir/FTC/TAF + TMP-SMX per ID. Pushed daily adherence, pill box given.
Tobacco - discussed, not ready.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Andre - A1c is about where it was, fine for now. Kidney number (creatinine) is 1.6, a touch higher than October. I'll recheck at your April visit along with a urine test. Nothing to change today.

Exam: BP and weight as charted. Heart and lungs normal. No pedal edema.

Labs back this afternoon: creatinine 1.6 again, eGFR in the high 50s. Urine microalbumin up to 520. UA 2+ protein, 1+ blood with a few RBCs.

1. CKD stage 3a - now two values more than 3 months apart under 60 with albuminuria and microscopic blood. Young for this and the blood makes me want a kidney specialist to look, not just call it diabetic. Nephrology referral placed. Continue lisinopril. Avoid NSAIDs.
2. DM2, HTN - unchanged.
3. HIV - per ID, adherence still spotty by his account.
RTC Sept for physical.

ID clinic follow-up, seen 06/07/2021.

On bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF and TMP-SMX DS daily since late November. Reports missing doses a few times a week, more when routines change. Feels well.

CD4 210. HIV-1 RNA 1,200 copies/mL - a large drop from baseline but not suppressed, consistent with partial adherence.

documents.author: PCP

Annual exam. 33M with HIV (on ART via ID), DM2, HTN, CKD 3a.

He never made the nephrology appointment. Asked him plainly; he says between ID, the pharmacist calls and this office he can't take another specialist right now and he feels fine. I explained why I wanted it (blood and protein in the urine at his age). He would rather we keep an eye on it here for now. Referral closed at his request; will revisit.

ROS otherwise negative. Smoking ~10/day. Alcohol rare. Sleeping ok, mood ok - PHQ-9 4.

Exam: BP as charted. HEENT normal, oropharynx without thrush. Neck no LAD, thyroid normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. GU deferred. Skin no rashes. Ext no edema. Monofilament intact both feet.

Prevention: flu, PCV20 (HIV indication) and Tdap today. COVID series done in spring. Eye exam in August, no retinopathy. HCV negative last fall.

Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, UA, urine microalbumin.

Plan: continue current meds. Cessation offered again. RTC 3-4 months.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Andre, cholesterol fine, liver tests fine, blood counts fine. Kidney function steady compared to spring. Urine protein still there (470), which is why the lisinopril matters - please don't skip it. A1c in range for you. See you in December.

documents.title: RE: pee is dark
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you wrote. No fever, vomiting or severe pain? If any of those, go to the ER. Otherwise I'd like you seen by the kidney specialists tomorrow - this is exactly the reason I've wanted them involved. I'm messaging the nephrology on-call now to get you a slot Monday. Drink normally, no ibuprofen or similar.

documents.body: no fever no throwing up. ok ill go tomorrow

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with nephrology on call. They will see him tomorrow at 2:30 in clinic. Texted pt the time and address. Faxing last 2 yrs of labs in the morning.

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEPHROLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Seen 07/17/2023 at the request of primary care.

CC: dark urine x 2 days.

HPI: 35-year-old man with HIV, type 2 diabetes, hypertension and CKD stage 3a with longstanding albuminuria and microscopic hematuria. He had an upper respiratory infection that cleared about a week ago; two days ago his urine turned dark and he has had a mild ache in the flank. On questioning he recalls a few similar spells over roughly the last three years, each after a cold, each clearing on its own; he never reported them. No NSAIDs or other new medications, no dysuria, no rash, no joint complaints.

Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF daily, TMP-SMX DS daily (ID).
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother with type 2 diabetes, father hypertension, a maternal uncle on dialysis (cause not known).
Social: smokes about 10 cigarettes a day; occasional alcohol; not working, previously in security.

Exam: BP 152/96. Comfortable. No rash, no joint swelling, no edema. No CVA tenderness to speak of.

Data: urinalysis with red cell casts on microscopy and proteinuria. Creatinine 1.8 (his baseline in your records 1.5-1.7). Serum albumin 3.9. 24-hour urine protein 2.1 g/day.

Impression: episodes of gross hematuria arriving a few days after upper respiratory infections, on a background of persistent microscopic hematuria and proteinuria, with active sediment - most consistent with IgA nephropathy. Albumin is preserved; not nephrotic.
Plan:
- Continue lisinopril.
- Repeat creatinine and urine protein in 4-6 weeks.
- Kidney biopsy if proteinuria rises or function declines.
- Avoid NSAIDs.
- Return in 6 months, sooner as needed.

Thank you for this referral.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back after nephrology. Urine went back to normal color within about 4 days. No flank pain now.

Read the nephrology letter with him: IgA nephropathy is their working diagnosis, biopsy if it gets worse. He's relieved there's a name for it. Plans to keep the 6-month nephrology appointment.

BP high again today. He says it's always up here. Lisinopril 20 continued as is.

Exam: RRR, lungs clear, no edema.

Labs today: CMP, CBC, UA, A1c (repeat requested by nephrology, results to them).
Updated problem list. RTC Oct for flu shot, Jan after nephrology.

documents.title: Nephrology Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology group - follow-up, seen 01/08/2024.

He returns six months after the clinical diagnosis of IgA nephropathy. For about two months his legs have been swelling progressively, and he notices foamy urine at times. No infections in the interval, no new drugs, no medication changes, no recreational drugs.

Other history: type 2 diabetes and hypertension on metformin and lisinopril; HIV on a bictegravir-based regimen with TMP-SMX prophylaxis through ID.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 145/90. Mild periorbital puffiness. Pitting edema 3+ both legs to the knees. Lungs clear.

Labs today: serum albumin 2.1, 24-hour urine protein 4.2 g, creatinine as attached, fasting glucose 130, A1c 7.2%. Hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis C antibody negative.

Assessment: nephrotic syndrome - heavy proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia and edema - in a patient with presumed IgA nephropathy. The picture has changed enough that tissue is needed.
Plan:
- Percutaneous kidney biopsy performed today under ultrasound guidance, left lower pole; no complications, observed and discharged. Pathology to follow.
- Furosemide 40 mg daily for edema; low-salt diet.
- Continue lisinopril.
- BMP in 2 weeks; return after pathology.

reports.text:
Specimen: native kidney, left, percutaneous needle core biopsy.
Light microscopy: cortex and medulla with adequate glomeruli for evaluation. Several glomeruli show segmental sclerosis with hyalinosis; the remaining glomeruli are unremarkable by light microscopy. Tubules, interstitium and vessels without specific diagnostic change.
Immunofluorescence and electron microscopy: no significant immune-complex deposition.
Comment: findings correlate with the clinical history of nephrotic-range proteinuria.
reports.conclusion: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis pattern of injury; no significant immune-complex deposition.

documents.title: Kidney Biopsy - Surgical Pathology
documents.author: pathology
documents.body:
Native kidney biopsy collected 01/08/2024, report signed 01/19/2024 and copied to primary care.
Diagnosis: focal segmental glomerulosclerosis pattern - segmental sclerosis and hyalinosis in some glomeruli, without significant immune-complex deposition. Full report attached.

conditions.label: Medication noncompliance
conditions.note: Antiretrovirals not taken for about 6 months

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in on his own after 5 months away. Legs swelling again for the past 2 weeks, urine foamy on and off.

He told me today he has not taken his HIV medicine at all for about 6 months, since around January. Ran out, didn't refill, then didn't want to face ID. TMP-SMX also mostly not taken. Still taking metformin, lisinopril, furosemide most days. Has not seen nephrology since January.

ROS: no fever, cough, dyspnea, chest pain, dysphagia, diarrhea, headache. Noticed some spots on his skin.

Exam: BP 150/95, wt 89 kg (86 in Feb). Not in distress. No periorbital edema today. Pitting edema both legs up to the knees. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Skin: scattered lesions on the trunk and arms, appearance consistent with an HIV-related opportunistic skin infection; organism not clear clinically. Mouth clear.

Office UA: 4+ protein. Microscopy with oval fat bodies.

A/P
1. Nephrotic syndrome / FSGS, IgA nephropathy, CKD 3a - edema recurring, likely worse with untreated HIV. CMP, CBC, A1c today. Will call with creatinine and contact nephrology.
2. HIV off ART x 6 months - CD4 today. Needs to be back with ID now; long talk, no lecture. He agreed to restart if we help him get in.
3. Skin infection, HIV-related - ID to evaluate at re-engagement.
4. Medication nonadherence - documented; case management referral through ID again.
5. HTN - above goal. Continue lisinopril 20 and furosemide 40.
Will call tomorrow.

orders.reason: HIV off ART 6 months, CD4 180, skin infection

documents.title: Creatinine and CD4 results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Creatinine 3.2 (was 1.6-1.9). CD4 180. Potassium ok.

AKI on CKD. Spoke with nephrology on call: they will move up his appointment; agree with restarting ART promptly through ID, keep up the furosemide, recheck labs. No urgent admission needed with normal potassium and no symptoms.

Called pt with all of this. He has not taken any ibuprofen. ID referral faxed marked urgent; clinic nurse will call him. Lab recheck end of August, video visit right after.

documents.title: ID appointment
documents.author: MA
documents.body: ID clinic scheduled pt Aug 12, 9:00. Pt informed and confirmed. Case manager there aware.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Re-engagement Visit
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
ID clinic, seen 08/12/2024 after a gap of about 14 months.

HIV-1 with poor adherence; reports no antiretrovirals since roughly January. Recent CD4 at primary care 180. HIV-1 RNA today 72,000 copies/mL.
Recent kidney course noted: FSGS on biopsy in January, nephrotic syndrome, creatinine 3.2 last month.

Exam: afebrile. Skin lesions on trunk and arms as described by primary care - HIV-related opportunistic skin infection; we will follow these here. Oropharynx clear. Lungs clear. Leg edema.

Plan:
- Restart bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF daily today with resistance testing sent. Kidney function will be watched closely.
- Restart TMP-SMX DS daily.
- Case manager re-assigned; weekly pharmacy delivery restarted.
- Return 4 weeks.

Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Venipuncture

events.reason: Follow-up of kidney function and HIV restart

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Holiday Monday; he asked for the video slot and I had time.

Restarted ART at ID on Aug 12, says he has taken it every day for three weeks, blister packs are coming weekly. TMP-SMX too. Swelling is down, now mostly at the ankles by evening. Urine still foamy. No fever, cough, diarrhea, headache. Skin spots unchanged, ID is following them.

Labs 8/29: creatinine 2.4, down from 3.2 in July but well above his 1.6-1.9 baseline. Potassium fine.

No vitals (video).

A/P
1. AKI on CKD 3a - improving; not back to baseline. Recheck with next visit. Nephrology appointment pending; reminded him.
2. HIV - back on bictegravir/FTC/TAF and TMP-SMX through ID. Keep going.
3. FSGS, IgA nephropathy, nephrotic syndrome - furosemide 40, lisinopril 20.
4. DM2 - metformin as before.
5. Skin infection - per ID.
RTC in person in 3 months with labs. Front desk to book.

documents.title: Follow-up scheduling attempt
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called to book 3 mo f/u per PCP. No answer, voicemail full. Sent portal message with scheduling link.

documents.title: Time for your follow-up
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Andre, this is the nurse from your primary care office. You're due for your kidney labs and a visit with the doctor, and your flu shot. Reply here or call and we'll find a time that works with your ride. We can also do the visit by video and arrange the labs separately.

documents.title: Refills: metformin, lisinopril, furosemide
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy refill requests x3. Not seen in person since July, overdue for labs. PCP approved 30-day supply each with note to pharmacy: patient must schedule visit/labs for further refills. Portal message from Nov unread.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Cavitary lesion in the right upper lobe. Remaining lungs clear. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal. Mediastinum not widened.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary clinic - consultation 01/06/2025, copy to primary care.

37-year-old man with HIV/AIDS, CKD stage 3, IgA nephropathy/FSGS, and an HIV-related skin infection under ID care, seen for three weeks of persistent cough with low-grade fevers, night sweats and about 10 pounds of weight loss. Increasingly tired. Antiretrovirals have been irregular again because of circumstances at home.

Meds as reported: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF, TMP-SMX, metformin, lisinopril, furosemide.
Allergies: NKDA. Smokes about 10 cigarettes daily.

Exam: T 38.2 C, HR 92, RR 20. Cachectic. Breath sounds diminished over the right upper lobe. No wheeze.

Data: CD4 180; viral load elevated per ID. Sputum AFB smear positive. Chest radiograph shows a cavitary lesion in the right upper lobe.

Impression: active pulmonary tuberculosis, smear-positive, cavitary.
Plan:
- Airborne precautions at home; mask.
- Reported to the state public health TB program for directly observed therapy; regimen to be coordinated with ID because of drug interactions with his antiretrovirals.
- Sputum cultures and susceptibilities pending.
- Follow-up here in 2 months.

documents.title: Pulmonology letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed pulmonology letter re active TB. Called pt - no answer; left message asking him to call, and that we want to see him once he's cleared to be around others. Called ID clinic: they are aware and coordinating with public health.

documents.title: TB Program Treatment Notice
documents.author: public health
documents.body:
State public health TB program - notice to primary care provider, dated 02/10/2025.

Re: Andre Palmer, DOB 10/24/1987.
Sputum culture from 01/06/2025 grew TB complex organisms, susceptible to isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol.
Treatment: directly observed therapy started with isoniazid, rifabutin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, with pyridoxine. Rifabutin chosen with the ID clinic, who adjusted his antiretroviral regimen for the interaction; details are in their records.
Please contact the program before prescribing new medications.

documents.title: Outreach call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called to check in and offer a visit; overdue for diabetes and kidney labs. Voicemail, message left with callback number. Pharmacy confirms metformin and lisinopril last filled in January.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside GI practice - consultation 07/08/2025.

Reason: painful swallowing.

37-year-old with AIDS, IgA nephropathy and FSGS, on treatment this year for pulmonary tuberculosis, with two weeks of pain on swallowing, about 10 pounds of weight loss and low-grade fevers. Antiretrovirals irregular. His HIV clinic gave him oral nystatin a week ago without improvement.

Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Exam: thin. Oral thrush on the tongue and palate. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Labs: hemoglobin 12.5, WBC 3.8, platelets 150K, CD4 50, HIV-1 RNA 120,000.

Impression: candidal esophagitis, presumed clinically given odynophagia with oral thrush and a CD4 of 50, failed topical therapy.
Plan:
- Fluconazole 200 mg once, then 100 mg daily for 21 days (dose reduced for kidney function); TB program and ID notified of the added drug.
- Endoscopy only if no response within 1 week.
- Restart and stay on antiretrovirals - ID to see him this month.

documents.title: TB Program Completion Notice
documents.author: public health
documents.body:
State public health TB program, 10/20/2025.
Andre Palmer has completed 9 months of directly observed therapy for drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis. Treatment completed. Case closed with the program. Any new respiratory symptoms should prompt re-evaluation.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED - visit 01/19/2026.

CC: diarrhea.
HPI: 38M with AIDS and poor antiretroviral adherence, IgA nephropathy with FSGS, CKD 3; candidal esophagitis last July and pulmonary TB last year (treatment completed). Three weeks of watery diarrhea with about 10 lb weight loss. Denies fever, blood in stool, recent travel.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: mild diffuse abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding. Mucous membranes dry.

Results: CD4 50. HIV-1 RNA 120,000. Stool culture: no Salmonella, Shigella or Campylobacter. Ova and parasites negative. Modified acid-fast stain of stool positive. C. difficile antigen negative.

ED course: IV fluids; tolerated oral fluids afterward.
Impression: cryptosporidiosis in advanced HIV, with dehydration.
Disposition: discharged home with oral rehydration instructions; ID clinic follow-up arranged within the week; antiretrovirals are the main treatment.

documents.title: ED follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after ED record received. Spoke with pt briefly; diarrhea a little better, drinking fluids, saw ID on Friday. Offered visit here, he said he'd call when he's feeling better. Encouraged him to.

events.reason: ED record and discharge summary received

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED - visit 04/06/2026.

CC: headache, fever, stiff neck.
HPI: 38M with AIDS (HIV for about five years, poor adherence), IgA nephropathy, CKD and cryptosporidiosis in January. Two weeks of headache, fever and neck stiffness, steadily worse despite acetaminophen.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: T 38.5 C, BP 110/70, P 100, RR 18.
Exam: lethargic, oriented to person, place and time. Neck stiff; meningeal sign positive on passive neck flexion. No focal neurologic deficit.

Labs: WBC 4.5, Hgb 12.2, Plt 210K. CD4 50. HIV-1 RNA 120,000.
Lumbar puncture: opening pressure 280 mm H2O. CSF WBC 22/uL, 90% lymphocytes; protein 100 mg/dL; glucose 20 mg/dL. Ink preparation positive for encapsulated yeast. Cryptococcal antigen positive.

Impression: cryptococcal meningitis with raised intracranial pressure.
Disposition: admitted to medicine, ID consulted.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital - discharge summary.
Admitted 04/06/2026, discharged 04/21/2026.
Principal diagnosis: cryptococcal meningitis.
Other: AIDS (CD4 50), CKD with FSGS/IgA nephropathy, type 2 diabetes, hypertension.

Course: induction with liposomal amphotericin B and flucytosine for 2 weeks, doses adjusted to kidney function with daily labs. Repeat lumbar punctures to relieve pressure, with headache improving after each. Fever resolved and he became more alert.

Discharge medications: fluconazole 400 mg daily for 8 weeks, then 200 mg daily until ID says otherwise. Home medications otherwise as before.
Antiretrovirals: to be restarted at the ID clinic about 4 to 6 weeks after induction began.
Follow-up: ID clinic 1 week; primary care when able.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Checking in after your hospital stay
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Andre, I got the hospital summary. I'm glad you're home. Whenever you're ready, I'd like to see you - by video is fine - to go over your kidney and diabetes medicines with the new ones. Just reply here.

reports.text: Pre- and post-gadolinium imaging of the brain. Multiple ring-enhancing lesions in the cerebral cortex. No hemorrhage. Ventricles normal in size. No midline shift.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record

Regional hospital ED - visit 07/21/2026.

CC: headache, fever, confusion.
HPI: 38M with AIDS and cryptococcal meningitis treated in April, brought in by his partner, who reports two weeks of worsening headache, fever and confusion; less responsive and having trouble walking.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: T 38.7 C. Neck stiff. Right-sided weakness.
Labs: CD4 50.
Imaging: MRI brain with multiple ring-enhancing lesions in the cerebral cortex.

Impression: cerebral toxoplasmosis.
Disposition: admitted to medicine, ID consulted.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital - discharge summary.
Admitted 07/21/2026, discharged 08/07/2026.
Principal diagnosis: cerebral toxoplasmosis.
Other: AIDS (CD4 50); cryptococcal meningitis (April 2026) on fluconazole; CKD with FSGS/IgA nephropathy; type 2 diabetes; hypertension.

Course: started pyrimethamine 200 mg once then 50 mg daily, sulfadiazine dosed to kidney function, and leucovorin 10 mg daily. Fever resolved; more alert day by day. Repeat MRI after 2 weeks showed the lesions smaller. Right-sided weakness improving with physical therapy.

Plan: complete 6 weeks of treatment, then maintenance per ID. Fluconazole continues. ID clinic in 1 week. Home with partner.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Call from partner
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt's partner called (pt on speaker, gave permission). Asking what follow-up he needs with us after the hospital. Offered next available video or office visit; partner wants to check the ID and PT schedule first and will call back. Hospital summary is in the chart for PCP.
